newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULFON FIRM PLANS SINGLE BALKAN PHONE CARD.
newsitem.headline: BULFON FIRM PLANS SINGLE BALKAN PHONE CARD.

text.p: Bulgarian-Greek joint telecom venture, Bulfon, is negotiating with other companies in the region to unify phone card systems for the Balkans, officials said on Wednesday.

"One of the main priorities of our 1997-1998 programme, discussed at Bulfon's shareholders meeting on Tuesday, is to develop Bulfon's activities (in the Balkan market)," Pericles Katsioulas, Managing Director of Greece's Intracom SA group, told Reuters.

"We will start work on unifying the phone card systems in the Balkans so that calls could be made with one card in any one of the Balkan countries," he said, adding that this was not only an economic but also a political issue.
Bulfon, which currently operates only in Bulgaria, uses Intracom's technology for the production of its chip cards for the Bulgarian phone card system.

A single system for the Balkans would mean unifying the codes on the cards, Katsioulas said. Talks are underway with Greek state telecommunications company OTE , Bulgaria's state telecoms company and Romania's Rom Telecom RA, he said.
Katsioulas said Intracom's technology for the production of such chip cards was used in Albania, Romania and Greece.

The Executive Director of the Bulgarian Telecommunications Company (BTC) Marian Dragostinov said Bulfon's shareholders had decided to raise BTC's share in the venture by two percent from 32 percent. Intracom will hold the remaining 66 percent.
The establishment of the Bulfon venture in November 1995 sparked a row in the local media because the BTC held only 32 percent of the venture, while Intracom held the majority stake.
"Now the BTC has a blocking share of 34 percent in the venture," Dragostinov told Reuters.

"Intracom, which has faced a lot of difficulties on the Bulgarian market, will continue to work for the modernisation of the Bulgarian telecommunications and is prepared to help in attracting foreign investments," Katsioulas said.

Bulfon has installed so far some 2,500 phone card machines in 34 towns in Bulgaria, investing $6.2 million so far. It plans to install a total of 25,000 phone card machines by 1999, investing more than $30 million.
